chapter_seo_title: Yu Wei Ascends, Ji Ning Descends – Karma Crashes the Party
chapter_meta_description: Yu Wei becomes a Celestial Immortal, only to learn Ji Ning was tricked into killing billions and is lost in the void. A bizarre stay of execution awaits him.
og_title: Yu Wei Ascends, Ji Ning Descends – Ch. 476
og_description: New Celestial Immortal Yu Wei arrives home to find her husband exiled into a void of endless storms. Meanwhile, Ji Ning discovers his enemy's weirdest training program yet.
twitter_description: She survived her tribulation, but the real trial awaits. Ji Ning is lost in the void, and a whole civilization of horned warriors just signed him up for 'eternal sparring partner' duty.

lore_anchors.definition: A type of tribulation that tests the cultivator's Dao-heart through psychological and emotional trials; the longest and most dangerous stage of the Heavenly Tribulation.
Miraculous phenomena that mark a successful Celestial Immortal ascension, signifying the cultivator's acceptance by the Heavenly Dao.
The periodic ordeals faced by cultivators below the Celestial Immortal stage, which cease upon true immortality.
An inescapable flame that burns the soul directly from within, triggered by extreme karmic sin; it bypasses physical and magical defenses.
A type of treasure born from the primordial energies of the universe, possessing unique and potent powers that often exceed standard magic treasures.
An innate spirit-treasure used by the Shaoyin clan to teleport Ji Ning out of the Grand Xia world and into the forbidden void.
The storm-ravaged, featureless void between the Three Realms and the wider Chaosverse; a hostile environment for cultivators reliant on Dao resonance.
An alien civilization of horned warriors, ruled by a Mother Queen, that exists within the Realm of Annihilation.
The absolute, supreme ruler of the Broken Horn World, whose will is law and whose command can override the instinctual behavior of her subjects.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Ji Ning's 'accidental' killing of ten billion mortals such a big deal?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the Desolate Era cosmology, the Heavenly Dao is an objective system of merit and sin. Intent is irrelevant; the objective act of mass slaughter creates an enormous karmic debt that the universe 'collects' in the form of Karmic Hellfire.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Can Yu Wei save Ji Ning?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. Lu Zu makes it clear that a Loose Immortal like himself is powerless. Only Ji Ning's true master, a Daofather, has any hope of searching the vast, trackless void to find him.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why are the horned warriors letting Ji Ning rest?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are under a direct command from their supreme ruler, the Mother Queen, who has ordered them to use him as a living combat training partner. They cannot kill him as long as she wants him alive.
